correctness.rationale: A tetrahedral simplex in a bipartite robust clique complex is a 4-set containing two vertex-disjoint edges (König); higher simplices are impossible, so H3=ker ∂3 is saturated in free C3. Exterior graded boundary gives ∂(z_Q∧z_R)=0 and all terms are valid disjoint edge pairs. Row-by-row square attachment yields a graph cycle basis of square boundaries. Edge attachment isolates two-new-vertex coefficients equal to old cycle basis; corner attachment isolates (e_u−e_v)∧z_i, injective over every field by the Koszul argument since u,v have at most one old common neighbor and are nonadjacent. Therefore pair products are independent mod every prime and rational. Filakovský’s prior wedge theorem gives rank binom(F,2) and freeness; field-uniform independence forces index one, hence primitive integral spanning. A planar symmetry multiplies every individual oriented square boundary by the same orientation sign; its square disappears in the wedge, so the integral action is unsigned on unordered pairs. Independently checked four finite grids, all boundaries and modular ranks; general proof is symbolic.
